slides.texte_overlay:
7 quiet habits that make
people take you more seriously
Following up in writing. After a call, a two-line email: "As agreed, I'll send the plan by Tuesday." Clear records make you look organised and reliable.
Keeping your phone off the table in meetings. Out of sight, not face down. Your full attention tells people their time and ideas genuinely matter to you.
Speaking about results, not effort. Not "I worked so hard on this" but "This saves the team three hours a week." Outcomes earn respect, complaints don't.
Being on time to the minute. Not early by half an hour, not late by five. Punctuality shows you respect other people's time and manage your own very well.
Knowing a little about many things. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and having real knowledge makes people trust what I say a bit more each time.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Real knowledge makes people trust what I say a bit more each time.

slides.texte_overlay: Asking one sharp question instead of five vague ones. "What's the biggest risk here?" One good question shows you understand more than a long speech.
Dressing one level above what's needed. A clean shirt on a casual day, polished shoes for a simple meeting. People take your words more seriously when you look prepared.
